subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Which mark of existence teaches that everything is impermanent?
explain: Anicca means impermanence and teaches that all things change.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is the Buddhist term for impermanence?
explain: Anicca is the teaching that everything is changing and impermanent.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: The mark of existence that teaches that life involves suffering or dissatisfaction is called ___.
explain: Dukkha refers to suffering
sets: dissatisfaction and the unsatisfactory nature of existence.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What does Anatta mean?
answer: no self|not-self|anatta|absence of a permanent self
explain: Anatta teaches that there is no permanent

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Name the three marks of existence.
answer: Anicca Dukkha Anatta|Anicca Dukkha and Anatta|impermanence suffering and no-self
explain: The three marks of existence are Anicca (impermanence)
sets: Dukkha (suffering or dissatisfaction) and Anatta (no permanent self).

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Anatta teaches that every person has an eternal and unchanging soul.
explain: Anatta teaches that there is no permanent and unchanging self or soul.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Explain why Anicca is important in Buddhist teachings.
answer: everything changes|nothing is permanent|attachment to things that change causes suffering
explain: Anicca teaches that everything changes. Understanding this can help Buddhists reduce attachment and suffering.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is the First Noble Truth?
options: The cause of suffering|The existence of suffering|The end of suffering|The path to end suffering
explain: The First Noble Truth teaches that dukkha exists and that life involves suffering or dissatisfaction.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is the Second Noble Truth?
answer: the cause of suffering|the origin of suffering|Samudaya|craving causes suffering
explain: The Second Noble Truth explains that the cause of suffering is craving or attachment.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is the Third Noble Truth?
answer: the end of suffering|cessation of suffering|Nirodha|suffering can end
explain: The Third Noble Truth teaches that suffering can cease when craving is eliminated.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is the Fourth Noble Truth?
answer: the path to end suffering|the way to end suffering|Magga|the Eightfold Path
explain: The Fourth Noble Truth teaches that the Eightfold Path is the way to end suffering.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Name the four Noble Truths in order.
answer: suffering cause of suffering end of suffering path to end suffering|Dukkha Samudaya Nirodha Magga
explain: The four Noble Truths are Dukkha
column17: its cessation and the path to its cessation.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: The Second Noble Truth identifies craving as a cause of suffering.
explain: Craving or tanha leads to attachment and suffering according to the Second Noble Truth.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Explain how the Four Noble Truths describe the problem of suffering and how it can be overcome.
model: 1 mark: Dukkha teaches that suffering or dissatisfaction exists. 1 mark: Samudaya identifies craving or attachment as its cause. 1 mark: Nirodha teaches that suffering can cease. 1 mark: Magga identifies the Eightfold Path as the way to end suffering.
explain: The Four Noble Truths explain that suffering exists
column14: can cease and can be overcome by following the Eightfold Path.
column15: The Four Noble Truths provide the Buddha's diagnosis of suffering and the way to liberation.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Which part of the Eightfold Path concerns understanding the Four Noble Truths?
explain: Right Understanding or Right View involves understanding the Four Noble Truths and Buddhist teachings.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Which part of the Eightfold Path involves speaking truthfully and avoiding harmful speech?
explain: Right Speech means communicating truthfully and avoiding lying

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Which part of the Eightfold Path teaches Buddhists to avoid harming living beings through their actions?
explain: Right Action involves behaving ethically and avoiding harmful actions.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Choosing work that does not harm others is known as Right ___.
explain: Right Livelihood means earning a living in an ethical way that avoids causing harm.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Name the three parts of the Eightfold Path that belong to wisdom.
answer: Right Understanding Right Intention|Right View Right Intention|Right Understanding and Right Intention
explain: The wisdom section consists of Right Understanding and Right Intention. The question asks for the two wisdom factors; the third mark is for identifying wisdom as a category.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Name the three parts of the Eightfold Path that belong to ethical conduct.
answer: Right Speech Right Action Right Livelihood|Right Communication Right Conduct Right Livelihood
explain: The ethical conduct section consists of Right Speech

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Name the two parts of the Eightfold Path that belong to mental discipline.
answer: Right Effort and Right Mindfulness|Right Mindfulness and Right Concentration|Right Effort Right Mindfulness Right Concentration
explain: Mental discipline includes Right Effort

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Name all eight parts of the Eightfold Path.
answer: Right Understanding|Right Intention|Right Speech|Right Action|Right Livelihood|Right Effort|Right Mindfulness|Right Concentration
model: 1 mark each for Right Understanding, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness and Right Concentration. Award up to 5 marks.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is the first of the Five Moral Precepts?
answer: refrain from taking life|do not kill|avoid killing living beings
explain: The first precept is to abstain from taking life or harming living beings.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Which precept teaches Buddhists not to take what has not been given?
options: Avoid intoxicants|Avoid false speech|Avoid stealing|Avoid sexual misconduct
answer: Avoid stealing|refrain from taking what is not given
explain: The second precept is to refrain from taking what has not been freely given.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What does the third Moral Precept ask Buddhists to avoid?
answer: sexual misconduct|misconduct in sexual relationships|harmful sexual behaviour
explain: The third precept teaches Buddhists to avoid sexual misconduct and harmful sexual behaviour.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What does the fourth Moral Precept teach Buddhists to avoid?
explain: The fourth precept is to abstain from false or dishonest speech.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: The fifth Moral Precept teaches Buddhists to avoid intoxicants that cause ___.
explain: The fifth precept is to avoid intoxicants that lead to heedlessness or loss of mindfulness.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Name all five Moral Precepts.
answer: refrain from taking life|refrain from stealing|refrain from sexual misconduct|refrain from false speech|refrain from intoxicants
model: 1 mark each for: not taking life, not stealing, avoiding sexual misconduct, avoiding false speech and avoiding intoxicants that cause heedlessness. Award up to 5 marks.
explain: The five precepts are to refrain from taking life
column15: false speech and intoxicants that cause heedlessness.
column16: The Five Moral Precepts are ethical guidelines that help Buddhists avoid harmful actions and develop a moral life.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Which perfection means generosity or giving?
explain: Dana is the perfection of generosity or giving.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is the perfection of moral discipline called?
explain: Sila means moral discipline or ethical conduct.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Which perfection means patience or forbearance?
explain: Khanti or Kshanti is the perfection of patience and forbearance.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is Virya in the Six Perfections?
explain: Virya is the perfection of energy
sets: effort and perseverance in Buddhist practice.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is Dhyana in the Six Perfections?
explain: Dhyana is the perfection of meditation and concentration.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: What is Prajna in the Six Perfections?
explain: Prajna is the perfection of wisdom or insight into the nature of reality.

subject: Theology And Philosophy
text: Name all six perfections in the Mahayana Buddhist tradition.
model: 1 mark each for Dana (generosity), Sila (morality), Khanti (patience), Virya (effort), Dhyana (meditation) and Prajna (wisdom). Award up to 5 marks.
explain: The six perfections are Dana
column17: The Six Perfections are qualities cultivated by Mahayana Buddhists on the path to enlightenment.
